title: Rate Law of Crystal Violet Fading Using Beer's Law
description: A semi-guided Chemistry investigation in which students design and obtain approval for wavelength, calibration, and kinetic choices; prepare four independent standards plus stock; collect time-coupled absorbance evidence; compare integrated rate laws; calculate w and k*; and complete teacher-configured waste treatment.
learningGoals: Design and justify a wavelength, blank, calibration range, and five-point Beer-Lambert calibration.
Collect fresh absorbance-time evidence for a 10. mL CV/NaOH reaction under hydroxide-excess pseudo-rate conditions while preserving dead time.
Determine w by comparing zero-, first-, and second-order integrated plots and calculate k* with correct sign and units.
safetyNotes: Wear a lab apron, splash-proof goggles, and disposable gloves while handling crystal violet and sodium hydroxide.
Crystal violet stains and 0.200 M sodium hydroxide is corrosive; wash skin contact with copious water.
Keep separate pipettes assigned to crystal violet, sodium hydroxide, and water.
Use 70% isopropyl alcohol for stained glassware only under the teacher's approved cleanup procedure.
Bleach remaining crystal violet with sufficient sodium hydroxide, then neutralize excess base with the teacher-approved acid before following the local disposal rule.
